nodes.name: CoNi-PBA coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: The binary Co–Ni Prussian blue analogue (PBA) (CoNi-PBA) cubes with the size of ∼70-80 nm were prepared via a coprecipitation method.
nodes.source_text: First, the binary Co–Ni Prussian blue analogue (PBA) (CoNi-PBA) cubes with the size of ∼70-80 nm were prepared via a coprecipitation method (Fig. S1a, ESI†).

nodes.name: PBA encapsulation electrospinning
nodes.procedure: The as-synthesized CoNi-PBAs were embedded into polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers via an electrospinning technology.
nodes.source_text: Then, the as-synthesized CoNi-PBAs were embedded into polyacrylonitrile (PAN) nanofibers (denoted as CoNi-PBAs@PAN-NFs) via an electrospinning technology (1st and 2nd plane of Scheme 1).

nodes.name: Space-confined calcination
nodes.procedure: The obtained CoNi-PBAs@PAN-NFs were calcinated at 500 °C under an air atmosphere for 2 h. During this process, the CoNi-PBA cubes thermally expanded outwards, while the PAN contracted inwards. This imparted a space confined effect of PAN on the CoNi-PBA-derived CoNiO_x NPs and thus the mutual extrusion and compressive stress of such NPs, which inevitably led to a rearrangement of metal atoms and lattice defects at the interconnected regions of two CoNiO_x NPs.

unit_operations.name: Calcination
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the obtained CoNi-PBAs@PAN-NFs were calcinated at 500 °C under an air atmosphere for 2 h.

nodes.source_text: Afterwards, the obtained CoNi-PBAs@PAN-NFs were calcinated at 500 °C under an air atmosphere for 2 h.

nodes.procedure: P dopants were introduced into CoNiOx-NFs via electrospinning technology (see the Experimental section).
nodes.source_text: For comparison, we also synthesized non-porous nanofibers containing defect-free CoNiO_x NPs (denoted as CoNiOx-NFs) via the technology of electrospinning (see the Experimental section)... we also doped a similar amount of P into CoNiO_x-NFs, and the sample of CoNiO_x-NFs with P dopants was denoted as CoNiO_x-P-NFs.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of D-CoNiOx-NFs displayed only peaks for Co3O4 (JCPDS no. 80-1541) and NiO (JCPDS no. 89-7130).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of D-CoNiOx-NFs displayed only peaks for Co3O4 (JCPDS no. 80-1541) and NiO (JCPDS no. 89-7130) (Fig. S4, ESI†).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show nanofibers composed of interconnected CoNiOx NPs with abundant channels/pores between interconnected NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a displays representative SEM images of D-CoNiOx-NFs, from which one can see nanofibers composed of interconnected CoNiOx NPs.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm nanofibers are highly porous and comprise interconnected CoNiOx NPs with diameter of 15-25 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding TEM images further confirm that the nanofibers are highly porous (red arrows) and comprise interconnected CoNiOx NPs with a diameter of 15-25 nm (Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals various crystal defects including stepped surface, twin-boundary as combination of NiO(111) and Co3O4(311)-oriented planes, micro-twin boundary and amorphous boundary.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice defects of CoNiOx NPs were further examined by using high-resolution TEM, indicating the presence of various crystal defects, such as a stepped surface, twin-boundary as a combination of NiO(111) and Co3O4(311)-oriented planes, micro-twin boundary and amorphous boundary (Fig. 1d and e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Co, Ni, and O elements in a single fiber.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping of a selected nanofiber signified the uniform distribution of Co, Ni, and O elements (Fig. 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XAFS spectra similar to Co3O4 indicate Co species in form of Co3O4; lower intensity of Co–O and tetrahedral Co–Co peaks for D-CoNiOx-NFs indicates presence of unsaturated Co cations, especially tetrahedral Co2+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge spectra of CoNiOx-NFs and D-CoNiOx-NFs are quite similar to that of Co3O4... the intensity of Co–O and tetrahedral Co–Co peaks for the D-CoNiOx-NFs is lower than that of CoNiOx-NFs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XAFS spectra similar to NiO indicate Ni species in form of NiO; markedly decreased intensity of Ni–Ni peak for D-CoNiOx-NFs indicates presence of unsaturated Ni cations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the case of the Ni K-edge spectra, the spectra of CoNiOx-NFs and D-CoNiOx-NFs are quite similar to that of NiO... The intensity of the Ni–Ni peak is markedly decreased for the sample of D-CoNiOx-NFs.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface area of D-CoNiOx-P-NFs is larger than CoNiOx-P-NFs with significantly enhanced mesoporous distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET surface area of CoNiOx-P-NFs and D-CoNiOx-P-NFs was then determined by the experiment of low-temperature N2 adsorption–desorption (Fig. S13, ESI†), which signified that the BET surface area of D-CoNiOx-P-NFs is larger than that of CoNiOx-P-NFs.

nodes.characterization_summary: D-CoNiOx-P-NFs has ECSA value of 83.8 cm², larger than CoNiOx-P-NFs (63.6 cm²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: D-CoNiOx-P-NFs had a ECSA value of 83.8 cm² larger than that of CoNiOx-P-NFs (63.6 cm²).
